newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini would be "surprised" by any EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini would be "surprised" by any EMU delay.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Tuesday he would be surprised if there were any delay to the launch of Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) and said Italy was committed to the project.

Asked whether, in the wake of political developments in France and Germany and Sweden's decision on Tuesday not to join EMU at the start, a delay was now looking more likely, Dini told a news conference: "I don't think so. I would be surprised."
"Obviously we have to wait for the new French government to outline clearly its objectives regarding the single currency," Dini said, after talks with his British counterpart Robin Cook.
"We are waiting to know the French position."
Analysts say a stunning victory by the left, which is sceptical of EMU and opposed to its fiscal strictures, in French elections at the weekend could delay or weaken EMU.

Fears over the health of the project have also been raised by a row between the German government and the Bundesbank over a plan by Bonn to revalue gold reserves and use some of the cash to help qualify for EMU.

Dini has in the past suggested that an extra year before the planned January 1, 1999 launch of EMU would have been beneficial to most countries as they struggle to beat their economies into line with the tough Maastricht Treaty criteria.
"Italy is not asking for a delay," Dini told the news conference. "Italy does not want there to be a delay."
He said that the Maastricht Treaty criteria could not be watered down, adding that if an attempt to do so were made "there would be no monetary union."

"The effort of all countries should be to seek to enter (into EMU) and to respect these parameters...But certainly it's not by watering down of the parameters that we can build monetary union," he said.
